product.title: Bow Sports Empire
product.summary: Five seasons of building a sports business, ending in an adaptive final round.
product.whatStudentsDo: Students name an empire and play five seasons — First Recruit through Championship Run — each choosing one of three strategy cards that move revenue, morale, efficiency and risk, reading an insight that names the concept behind the result, then spending earned coins. A five-question adaptive round closes it out.

facilitation.notes: One experience in two media. The Sheets build records evidence and emails claim codes; the browser build keeps state in the session only.

studentDataProfile.notes: State kept in browser localStorage only; no server call observed.

governance.maturityBasis: Both builds complete; browser build is polished and publicly reachable. No student-run evidence exists.

health.technicalBasis: Playtested end to end 2026-08-16 across two full runs. The best-looking simulation in the account and genuinely responsive — the flashy recruit moved revenue 20 to 25, morale 50 to 60, efficiency 30 to 25 and risk 20 to 35, with the information-asymmetry lesson named explicitly. The managed stats do not reach the grade.
knownBlockers: The final tier is driven by the 15-question quiz, not by the four stats the student spends the whole game managing. An all-risky run and an all-safe run ended with clearly different stats (morale 75 against 100, risk 30 against 20) and the identical D-TIER grade, so optimising the economy is optional.
Season 1 opens on generic startup copy — juggling product development and customer churn — under the sports-empire skin.

curation.tierBasis: The best-looking simulation in the account, and genuinely responsive to choices. The final grade currently ignores the four stats the student spends the game managing.

provenance.evidence: 201-M3-ECON/js/game-data.js season titles ('First Recruit', 'Scaling Up', 'Building the Machine', 'Storm Season', 'Championship Run') match CHAPTER_NARRATIVES in the repo's 'apps script' verbatim.
